# Results -- Study 532 (Firm-Age-Anomaly) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: proxy firm age from
each name's first available price date; each month sort the mixed-vintage basket into age
terciles, go long the OLD tercile and short the YOUNG tercile (old-minus-young), enter at the
close one day after the ranking is public, hold equal-weight to the next rebalance. Inference =
Newey-West HAC one-sample t on the monthly long-short, plus a firm-age label-shuffle placebo.
As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 10432 days x 40 tickers | `823c8d7707e9` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 8390 days | `c3b449e6ee7f` |
| Period covered | 1985-01-02 -- 2026-05-29 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close (auto_adjust=True). Universe: 39 large-caps with
data (1 of 40 candidates, SQ, returned no data and is dropped), deliberately spanning four
decades of IPO/listing vintages -- old-economy names whose price history begins at the
yfinance 1985 floor (AAPL, XOM, KO, JNJ...) down to recent IPOs (META 2012, UBER/ZM 2019,
SNOW/PLTR/DASH/ABNB 2020, RBLX/COIN 2021). Firm age = (rebal date - first price date) in years.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is names still trading in 2026. Young
firms that IPO'd and then failed/delisted -- exactly the names the new-list effect says should
underperform *worst* -- are absent. The surviving young names are the spectacular winners
(NVDA-era IPOs, META, etc.), so the short (young) leg is biased toward *over*-performers. This
pushes the old-minus-young spread **downward / negative**. The result below should be read with
that mechanism front of mind.

**Data limitation (named explicitly):** yfinance price history begins in 1985, so all
pre-1985-listed names share the same first-price-date and the age proxy collapses their
dispersion before ~2005. Genuine cross-sectional age dispersion only emerges once the recent
IPOs enter (post-2012). We report both the full sample and the clean post-2012 subsample.

## The honest test -- old-minus-young long-short

Each month: rank eligible names (>= 126 trading days of history) by firm age; long the oldest
tercile, short the youngest tercile, equal-weight, one-day execution lag, hold to next rebalance.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 490 (1985-07 -- 2026-04) |
| Mean return (annualised) | **-18.22%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 23.50%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.775 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-4.661** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 38.8% |
| Max drawdown | -100.0% (effective total loss by compounding) |

- The old-minus-young spread is **strongly negative**: old firms *under*-perform young firms by
  **18.2%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-4.661**. This is the **opposite sign** of the claimed new-list
  effect (Fama-French 2004 / Jiang-Lee-Zhang 2005 predict old > young).
- The sign reversal is the survivorship mechanism made visible: the young firms that survived to
  2026 are the winners; their failed peers are gone from the tape.

### Legs

| Leg | Mean (ann) | Avg firm age |
|---|--:|--:|
| Old tercile (long) | +15.74%/yr | 20.9 yrs |
| Young tercile (short) | +33.96%/yr | 8.7 yrs |
| SPY (market) | +12.65%/yr | -- |

### Clean post-2012 subsample (genuine age dispersion)

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 172 (2012 -- 2026) |
| Mean (ann) | -15.8%/yr |
| HAC t-stat | -2.067 |

Both windows agree: old-minus-young is significantly **negative**.

## Costs (one-way bps x turnover + borrow on the short leg)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Avg two-sided turnover / rebalance | 0.02 (terciles are near-static) |
| Transaction cost assumption | 10 bps one-way x turnover |
| Borrow assumption (short young leg) | 100 bps/yr |
| Net mean (annualised) | **-19.24%/yr** |
| Net HAC t-stat | -4.924 |
| Net Sharpe | -0.819 |

Costs are tiny here (turnover ~0.02) because age ranks barely move month-to-month -- the
old-minus-young portfolio is nearly a static bet. Net and gross are essentially identical; the
negative result is not a cost artefact.

## Robustness -- firm-age label-shuffle placebo

Permute which name is "old" vs "young" (200 shuffles) and rebuild the long-short. Under the null
(age carries no return info), shuffled means should be as large as the real one about as often.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real AGE mean (monthly) | -1.518% |
| Placebo mean of shuffles | -0.036% (std 0.474%) |
| Two-sided permutation p | **0.010** (over 200 shuffles) |

The real spread sits far in the tail of the shuffle null (p = 0.010): the age labels carry a
*genuine* signal -- it just points the wrong way for the claim under test.

## Synthetic positive control (faithful-engine / power check ONLY)

Plant a known age premium (old > young) on a deterministic panel; the engine must recover it,
seed-robustly, and return ~0 under the null. Averaged over 25 seeds:

| Planted premium | Avg AGE mean | Avg HAC t | Frac seeds t>2 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | -0.08%/yr | -0.026 | 0% |
| 0.05 | +1.53%/yr | +0.403 | 8% |
| 0.15 | +4.76%/yr | +1.221 | 12% |
| 0.30 | +9.58%/yr | +2.249 | 60% |

The engine is faithful: mean and t-stat rise monotonically with the planted premium and the null
is centred on zero. *This control proves the machinery, not the market -- it is never cited for
the real-tape stamp.*

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE (claimed premium).** The new-list effect as stated (old firms beat young
  firms, old-minus-young > 0) **does not appear**: the real-tape spread is significantly
  *negative* (-18.2%/yr, HAC *t* = -4.66; post-2012 *t* = -2.07; placebo p = 0.010). The
  claimed positive firm-age premium is absent on this basket; what shows up is its survivorship
  shadow. Literature support cannot rescue a sign that is reversed in the data.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Sharpe -0.775 (net -0.819), max drawdown -100% (effective total
  loss by compounding a persistently-losing long-short), hit rate 38.8%. As specified
  (old-minus-young) it loses money relentlessly; flipping the sign would be data-mining the
  survivor basket, not trading a premium.
- **Direction vs the claim -- BUSTED.** The Fama-French / Jiang-Lee-Zhang prediction (mature >
  young) is reversed here because the basket only contains young firms that *survived* -- the
  winners. The honest lesson is the bias, not a tradable edge in either direction.
